Subject: Velox Health — capacity overlay & cutover sprint for hosted->dedicated

James — thanks again for the call this morning. Per our discussion, I sketched a capacity overlay and a conservative cutover sprint for the hosted->dedicated migration so we can validate throughput without impacting Production SLAs. High-level asks: share 2 weeks of peak-hour token profiles (samples for user-facing chat vs. background embeddings), confirm blackout windows for deployment, and confirm who owns VPN/KMS network tests on your side.

Attached: velox_capacity_overlay_v1.xlsx (spreadsheet) — includes projected GPU vCPU mapping, sustained tokens/sec targets, and three test phases: smoke, load, and soak.

Proposed cutover sprint (week view):
- Day 0: Preflight — cluster provisioning, SSH/KMS handshakes, and model variant pinning
- Day 1: Smoke — single rack, 1% of traffic routing to Dedicated (validation of token correctness + latency SLO)
- Day 2: Load — ramp to 30%, run stress profiles, validate KV cache warm-paths
- Day 3: Soak — 72-hour soak at 60% with autoscale triggers active
- Day 4: Final swap window — increment to 100% with rollback gates and fallback routing policy ready

Key validation gates: end-to-end latency <= 250ms p95 for chat, <12% cost delta vs hosted baseline for steady-state, and no degradation on sensitive user flows. We recommend a two-hour quiesce window for cutover and a 1-hour rolling rollback capability.

Can you confirm procurement timeline and the right contact for a signed amendment (DocuSign)? If you can get us the peak token matrix by EOD Thu we’ll lock the provisioning plan with infra and schedule the hardware commission.

— Karthik

James — appreciate the sample. Quick answers inline and a small update to the overlay:

1) Autoscale & soak behavior: by default we enable autoscale on the Dedicated pool to add replica lanes up to your committed capacity. During soak we keep routing within Dedicated until the autoscale ceiling is hit. If latency climbs above SLO during autoscale lag, the routing policy will start sending excess traffic back to Hosted as a graceful degradation (this is our standard fallback policy).

2) Rollback latency: with warm KV caches and prefix pre-warming we estimate failover to Hosted in ~45–90s for in-flight traffic. Without pre-warm the worst-case could be 3–6 minutes while caches repopulate. That is why the smoke and load phases include cache-warm runs.

Updates made to velox_capacity_overlay_v1.xlsx: added a thermal headroom column (GPU util buffer) and a short-latency SLA column. Also attached a first-pass cutover runbook (velox_cutover_runbook_v1.pdf).

Next steps I propose:
- You confirm blackout window (Sat 04:00–08:00 UTC OK?) and signoff on runbook
- Procurement sends amendment skeleton for us to review by Tue 22 Feb
- We schedule provisioning window with infra for Wed 23 Feb (hardware commit), subject to procurement sign-off

If that timeline works I’ll lock in the infra ticket and book a 60-minute cutover rehearsal (dry run) the week prior.

— Karthik

James — technical ops notes from our side to make the rehearsal crisp:

Preflight checklist (infra):
- Provision Dedicated pool with n1-standard GPU topology matching velox_capacity_overlay_v1.xlsx
- KMS handshake, test signing of short-lived tokens, and verify HSM logs
- Ensure egress rules and BGP peerings for the VPC are established

Smoke/load test plan (validation steps):
- Smoke: single-node inference validations, deterministic sample prompts, token stream integrity check
- Load: 1-hour ramp from 0->30% with synthetic traffic matching the 95th percentile token length distribution you provided
- Soak: run production request replay at 60% sustained for 72 hours, monitor p95 latency, error-rate, and memory remnant for the KV cache

Acceptance gates before final swap:
- p95 latency <= 250ms (chat flow) for 72-hour soak
- Error rate < 0.3% sustained during load and soak tests
- Confirmation of successful failover rehearsal under simulated autoscale lag

Rollback plan (if acceptance fails):
- Execute immediate traffic shift to Hosted (pre-configured policy)
- Hold for 1 hour while Redwood infra rolls back model variant pin and drains to last-known-good nodes
- Post-mortem cadence: 48-hour incident review with assigned owners

I’ll own the rehearsal script + the runbook updates. Ben will coordinate the RBAC checks and access lists. Happy to run the dry-run on Fri 18 Feb (UTC-friendly window) if you can confirm stakeholders.

Best — Marissa
